# Tina4 PHP

> Tina4 PHP (`tina4stack/tina4php` on Packagist) is a web framework for PHP 8.2+ with zero runtime dependencies beyond `ext-json`: routing, ORM, Frond (Twig-compatible) templates, JWT auth, sessions, queues, WebSocket, GraphQL, WSDL/SOAP and Swagger are all built in. It is one of four Tina4 backends (Python, PHP, Ruby, Node.js) that share the same project layout, CLI, template syntax and `.env` variables.

Quick start. Install the Rust `tina4` CLI (`curl -fsSL https://tina4.com/install.sh | sh`, `brew install tina4stack/tap/tina4`, or `irm https://tina4.com/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows), then:

```bash
tina4 init php my-app   # the path is required; runs composer install for you
cd my-app
tina4 serve             # http://localhost:7145 (TINA4_PORT overrides)
```

Add a route by dropping a file in `src/routes/` (auto-discovered):

```php
<?php
use Tina4\Router;

Router::get("/api/hello/{name}", function ($request, $response) {
    return $response->json(["message" => "Hello, " . $request->params["name"]]);
});
```

Gotchas an agent most needs:

- GET routes are public; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE require a bearer token (or form token) by default. Chain `->noAuth()` to open a write route and `->secure()` to protect a GET.
- Routes are registered statically (`Router::get(...)`), never on an instance. Path parameters are read from `$request->params["name"]`; a typed placeholder such as `{id:int}` converts the value.
- `$response->json($data, $status)` and `$response->render("page.twig", $data)` are the usual returns; `$response($data)` also works.
- The entry point is `index.php`: `$app = new \Tina4\App(); $app->run();`.
- ORM models extend `\Tina4\ORM` and set `$tableName` and `$primaryKey`; camelCase properties map to snake_case columns automatically (`$autoMap`). Serialise with `toArray()` or `toDict()` (there is no `asArray()`).
- The database comes from `TINA4_DATABASE_URL` (`sqlite:///`, `postgres://`, `mysql://`, `mssql://`, `firebird://`). Change schema only through SQL files in `migrations/`, never in route code.
- The package's own CLI is `tina4php` (`vendor/bin/tina4php`); the `tina4` CLI forwards `tina4 generate <model|route|crud|migration|...>` to it. Generated write routes are secure by default.

## Docs

- [Quick reference](https://tina4.com/php/index.md): one-page cheat sheet of every feature
- [Getting started](https://tina4.com/php/01-getting-started.md): install, scaffold, project layout, first route
- [Routing](https://tina4.com/php/02-routing.md): methods, path parameters, route groups, auth modifiers, wildcards
- [Request and response](https://tina4.com/php/03-request-response.md): request fields, response helpers, status codes, validation, uploads
- [Templates](https://tina4.com/php/04-templates.md): Frond template engine, filters, inheritance
- [Database](https://tina4.com/php/05-database.md): configuration, parameterised queries, transactions, migrations, seeding
- [ORM](https://tina4.com/php/06-orm.md): models, CRUD, relationships, eager loading, soft delete, auto-CRUD
- [Authentication](https://tina4.com/php/08-authentication.md): JWT tokens, password hashing, login flow, protecting routes, CSRF
- [Middleware and security](https://tina4.com/php/10-middleware-security.md): the middleware pipeline, built-in and custom middleware
- [Queues](https://tina4.com/php/12-queues.md): producers, consumers, retries, dead letters, backends
- [Scaffolding](https://tina4.com/php/19-scaffolding.md): `tina4 generate` generators
- [CLI](https://tina4.com/php/31-cli.md): every `tina4` and `tina4php` command
- [Environment variables](https://tina4.com/php/33-environment-variables.md): the `.env` reference
- [Deployment](https://tina4.com/php/34-deployment.md): production config, Docker, health checks, reverse proxy, scaling
- [Release notes](https://tina4.com/php/36-releases.md): what changed in each release
- [Upgrading from v2](https://tina4.com/php/37-upgrading-from-v2.md): migration guide from Tina4 PHP v2
